summary: The denominator, missing-age, and two-sided contradiction fixes are coherent, and the revised linkage numbers trace correctly into the draft. The most important remaining problem is that the paper still claims improved transcription quality without adjudicated names; it also interprets validation rates computed on changing linked samples as evidence about marginal links. Core model-performance figures remain unreproducible because their producing ML code is absent.

findings.title: The headline claims improved transcription quality without any adjudicated name truth
findings.what_the_code_does: The code counts agreement with the two commercial transcriptions, for example `namefrst==namefrst_ml & namelast==namelast_ml_ditto` and the analogous FamilySearch expression. It never compares the model output with a blinded, adjudicated reading of the census image. The draft itself concedes at lines 279-305 that these are resemblance measures and that no adjudicated comparison exists, but still says the method “improves name transcription,” “systematically improve[s] transcription quality,” and has demonstrated that conclusion.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the paper's central claim, not a labeling detail. Agreement and improved linkage can arise from shared conventions or shared errors—especially the explicitly acknowledged FamilySearch/ditto asymmetry—so the available results do not establish that names are more accurate.
findings.how_to_check: Draw a fixed random sample stratified by commercial-transcription agreement and model-output status, blind adjudicators to source, independently transcribe the images, and tabulate exact-name and character error rates for Ancestry, FamilySearch, and the model.
findings.suggested_fix: Until an adjudicated sample exists, replace claims of improved transcription accuracy or quality throughout with the narrower verified claims: improved agreement with commercial transcriptions and improved linkage outcomes. Retain the explicit caveat already present at lines 279-305.

findings.title: Aggregate middle-initial rates over different linked samples do not validate the additional links
findings.what_the_code_does: The census analysis separately defines `validated_before` among `linked_before==1` and `validated_after` among `linked_after==1`, then compares their two conditional means. The mortality script similarly computes middle-initial agreement over every old-name link and every new-name link after separate `keep` operations. Neither calculation isolates links added by the new transcription or holds the linked population fixed, despite the mortality prose calling the result a check “on the additional links.”
findings.why_it_matters: Improved transcription changes who enters the linked sample. An aggregate validation rate can rise because retained or newly selected records have different middle-initial availability or difficulty even if the marginal added links are poor. Thus the reported percentages are descriptive composition changes and do not by themselves support the claims that the new links are true rather than spurious.
findings.how_to_check: Merge old and new link files by source and target IDs, classify pairs as retained, added, removed, or changed, and tabulate middle-initial availability and agreement separately for each class. For changed links, compare the old and new proposed partners on the same source person.
findings.suggested_fix: Report validation separately for retained, added, removed, and changed links, including middle-initial availability in each group. Reword the existing aggregate comparisons as descriptive until the added-link results are available.

findings.title: The reported 97–99% model-performance figures have no producing code in the package
findings.what_the_code_does: The claim registry marks the first-name, last-name, prose, and appendix performance figures as `status = "nocode"` with empty expressions such as `values = ["", ""]`. The checker turns each empty expression into `UNCHECKED`, and its documented behavior deliberately does not fail the run for unchecked claims. Consequently, a successful claim-check run cannot reproduce or verify these figures.
findings.why_it_matters: These are the paper's primary reported model-evaluation results. A replicator cannot recover the test split, normalization rules, sequence metric, character denominator, or the four percentages, and stale or differently defined figures would pass the current automated check.
findings.how_to_check: Run `rg -n 'table1-accuracy|appendix-accuracy|status = "nocode"' replication/claims.toml` and inspect `replication/claims_report.md`; the claims appear as unchecked rather than matched to generated results.
findings.suggested_fix: Archive the exact test-set construction and evaluation code, dependency versions, model checkpoint or deterministic inference outputs, and a generated result file containing all four raw metrics. Point `claims.toml` to those generated keys and make missing ML results fail the replication run.

verified_clean.item: Missing numeric ages are now excluded explicitly from both age-8-plus linkage denominators.
verified_clean.evidence: The ABE/JW script uses `keep if age >= 8 & !missing(age)` at LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do:43-46, and HLINK uses the same guard at LINKAGE/code/02_hlink/linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:186-191.

verified_clean.item: HLINK numerators are restricted to the same population used in their denominators for coverage, quality, and pair-change calculations.
verified_clean.evidence: The denominator datasets are constructed at LINKAGE/code/02_hlink/linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:218-230 and merged with `keep(3)` before counts at lines 291-303, 329-349, and 397-405.

verified_clean.item: The mortality numerator is now restricted to BUNMD men born by 1940 before counts and validation rates are calculated.
verified_clean.evidence: The filtered denominator is created and asserted unique at LINKAGE/code/03_mortality/05_make_linkage_table.do:38-60; every matched file is merged into it with `keep(3)` at lines 75-89.

verified_clean.item: The revised contradiction classification checks both members of a proposed link and forms mutually exclusive verified, unverifiable, and contradicted categories under the stated one-to-one truth mapping.
verified_clean.evidence: The reverse truth map is asserted unique at LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do:104-117 and LINKAGE/code/02_hlink/linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:257-270. Classification uses both merges at LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do:194-203 and LINKAGE/code/02_hlink/linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:340-349; the committed table counts sum to their linked-pair totals.

verified_clean.item: The revised linkage and mortality numbers in the draft match the generated tables registered by the claim checker.
verified_clean.evidence: The mortality claims are mapped to generated table cells at replication/claims.toml:500-547, while replication/claims_report.md:46 and replication/claims_report.md:72-74 record matches for the 7.08% gain, exact and conservative rates, and middle-initial percentages.

verified_clean.item: The extraction tool now includes all five linkage tables and fails when any regenerated raw-byte hash differs from its committed reference.
verified_clean.evidence: The complete table list and SHA-256 comparison are at replication/extract_deaglan_tables.py:49-75; the accumulated failure status is propagated at lines 124-159.

review_limits: The external datasets were unavailable, so the Stata pipeline could not be rerun. Counts, uniqueness assertions, and reported effects were assessed from source and committed generated outputs rather than independently recomputed from microdata.

The draft and its generated linkage tables were readable in the separate paper repository, but that repository was not the reviewed Git commit range; paper line references describe its current on-disk version.
This was a diff-scoped review of aae3252..0f6b466 plus the claims those changes feed. Unchanged analysis code outside the traced pipelines was not comprehensively re-audited.

The independence and construction of `mlp_training1930_1940.dta` could not be established from the available data. The review therefore does not certify that the FamilySearch-derived reference links are independent of HLINK training or model development.
